title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans Auditorium on 1969-06-28
lineage: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > DAT > DAT > ZA2 > Soundforge > .wav > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy June 28 ‘69 show captured on a solid soundboard tape; standout country‑folk moments like “Doin’ That Rag” with pedal steel and superb Pigpen blues, all presented with very good (if not pristine) audio.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its energetic, country‑inflected arrangements, tight playing across styles, and a legendary Pigpen showcase. Reviewers note the soundboard source delivers clear, listenable sound despite occasional hiss or slight EQ quirks, making this a highly recommended recording of a pivotal transitional period for the Dead.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 5‑star, highlighting exceptional musical moments and generally good soundboard audio; only minor recording complaints keep the rating just below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall mix with occasional background hiss on the Ogg version and a slight brightness/dullness variance likely due to cassette Dolby‑B handling; still very listenable.

standout_songs: Sitting On Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: A transitional, country‑folk set that blends early Workingman's Dead material with blues and ballads; tight pacing and energetic delivery throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Featured on pedal steel for “Doin' That Rag”, delivers fiery licks on “Sitting On Top of the World” and vocals on “Me and My Uncle”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s B‑3 organ work praised; overall keyboard texture supports the country‑folk vibe.
